Likelihood profile across one or more parameter cells

Source: R/9-profile.R
profile.Rceattle.Rd

Re-fits an Rceattle model while holding selected cells of a parameter fixed. Profiles a single cell (R_log_sd[species = 1]) or crosses several, such as log_M1[1, 1, 1] against log_M1[1, 2, 1] for residual M in males versus females. For each grid point the targeted cells are fixed in the TMB map and everything else is re-estimated.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'Rceattle'
profile(
  fitted = NULL,
  param = NULL,
  slots = NULL,
  values = NULL,
  transform = "log",
  cores = NULL,
  getsd = NULL,
  joint = c("none", "multiply", "add", "value"),
  ...
)

Arguments

fitted

an Rceattle model fit using fit_mod

param

Name of the parameter to profile: a raw slot in Rceattle$estimated_params, or one of the natural-scale aliases "sigmaR", "R_sd", "M1", "R0", "alpha", "beta", "q". See Details.

slots

A list of integer index vectors, one per cell to fix, each as long as the resolved parameter has dimensions: 1 for R_log_sd, 2 for rec_pars, 3 for log_M1. The "R0"/"alpha"/ "beta" aliases take the species index alone. So list(c(1, 1, 1), c(1, 2, 1)) crosses the two sex cells of species 1. If omitted it defaults to a single species-1 cell shaped to the parameter and warns, which requires length(values) == 1L.

values

A list of numeric vectors, one per entry of slots. The grid is expand.grid(values), so k slots give a k-D cross-profile.

transform

How user values map onto the internal scale before substitution: "log" (default), "identity", or a unary function such as qlogis, applied element-wise.

cores

Cores for the parallel fits. NULL (default) picks parallel::detectCores() - 6, capped at 2 under R CMD check; 1 forces sequential.

getsd

Whether each grid fit runs TMB::sdreport. The profile reads only nll, so FALSE is faster and changes nothing. NULL (default) inherits the input model's setting (TRUE only if it holds an sdrep).

joint

How the grid moves the cells in slots: "none" (default), "multiply", "add" or "value". See Details.

...

Unused; present for consistency with the stats::profile generic.

Value

A list of class "Rceattle_profile" with elements:

Rceattle_list

the fitted models, one per grid row, NULL where a fit did not converge so positions stay aligned with grid.

grid

grid values on the user scale, one column per profiled cell, named slot_1, slot_2, ...

nll

joint negative log-likelihoods, NA where the fit did not converge.

param

the profiled parameter name.

slots

the slots list, echoed for plotting.

alias

the natural-scale name asked for, or NA. Profiling "M1" returns param = "log_M1" because the model estimates M on the log scale, while grid holds the M values supplied, so a figure can label the axis in the units profiled.

joint

the mode used, so a figure can say whether grid holds a multiplier, an offset or a value.

Printing it reports whether the grid brackets the minimum; see print.Rceattle_profile.

Details

Natural-scale aliases. An alias implies transform = "log" and, for rec_pars, fills in the column so slots needs only the species index. transform is ignored with a warning when an alias is used. A raw slot instead has slots index the full array and transform set the scale.

"sigmaR", "R_sd"

R_log_sd

"M1"

log_M1

"R0", "alpha", "beta"

rec_pars columns 1, 2 and 3

"q"

index_log_q, base catchability, one entry per fleet; slots takes a fleet index or name. Fleets sharing a Catchability_index share one q, so naming any of them profiles the group: the rest are added with a message and joint becomes "value".

Joint modes. A joint mode profiles a vector-valued parameter such as an empirical age-based M, where "none" over ten ages and 13 values would be 13^10 fits.

"none"

(default) each slot gets its own grid and they cross.

"multiply"

one grid multiplying every cell, so the schedule keeps its shape; 1 is the fitted model.

"add"

one grid added to every cell, so the schedule keeps the differences between cells; 0 is the fitted model.

"value"

one grid; every cell takes that value.

A joint mode needs values to be one vector, and "multiply"/"add" work in natural units, so transform must be "log" or "identity". A value that would take a log-scale parameter to zero or below is an error naming the cell, not a failed fit.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(BS2017SS)
ss_run <- fit_mod(data_list = BS2017SS, inits = NULL, file = NULL,
    estimateMode = 0, random_rec = FALSE, msmMode = 0, avgnMode = 0,
    phase = FALSE, verbose = 0)
#> Warning: Passing ‘phase’, ‘verbose’ directly to fit_mod() is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Bundle these into fit_control() instead, e.g. fit_control(phase = ..., verbose = ...). Forwarding for now.
#> `age_trans_matrix` data does not span range of age for species 1 will fill with 0s

# 1-D profile of sigmaR for species 1, natural scale via the alias
p1 <- profile(ss_run, param = "sigmaR", slots = list(1),
    values = list(seq(0.1, 1.5, by = 0.1)))

# 2-D cross-profile of M1 across species 1 and 2 (sex 1, age 1)
p2 <- profile(ss_run, param = "M1",
    slots  = list(c(1, 1, 1), c(2, 1, 1)),
    values = list(seq(0.1, 0.4, length.out = 3),
                  seq(0.1, 0.4, length.out = 3)))

# An empirical age-based M moved as a whole: one slot per age bin on ONE grid
# of multipliers, so the schedule keeps its shape and 1 is the fitted model.
sp <- 1
p3 <- profile(ss_run, param = "M1",
    slots  = lapply(seq_len(ss_run$data_list$nages[sp]),
                    function(a) c(sp, 1, a)),
    values = list(seq(0.6, 1.4, by = 0.05)),
    joint  = "multiply")
# }
# Profiling catchability by fleet name, and reading a profile for where the
# data disagree, are in vignette("model-diagnostics").
